name: National Catholicism
summary: National Catholicism fused Spanish national identity with the Catholic Church as the basis of the state. It made Catholic doctrine the inspiration of law, gave the Church control over education, marriage and morals, and rejected liberal democracy, class struggle and secularism in favour of an authoritarian, hierarchical, corporatist order under a providential leader.
scope: The Francoist Spanish form, 1939-1975, as expressed in the Fundamental Laws (Fuero de los Españoles, Principles of the National Movement), the 1953 Concordat and scholarship on the regime. It represents the clerical-traditionalist pillar of Francoism, not Falangist national syndicalism, and excludes similar movements elsewhere (Ustase, French Fédération Nationale Catholique).

sources.usedFor: Regime practice: women, censorship, language, economy, repression, army.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The regime built a contributory social insurance system and Catholic charity, but the sources document no commitment to state-guaranteed universal care; inferred as split.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The Labour Fuero set a minimum wage but subordinated labour conditions to the national interest; no push for substantial raises is documented.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The regime pursued autarky and state direction after 1939 and only liberalized late in the 1950s under technocrats, so adherents did not hold that markets beat governments.

public-ownership.rationale: The state ran strategic industry through autarkic policy, but National Catholic doctrine itself did not demand public ownership; adherents split.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Property was protected as a right with a social function, and nothing documents a call for significantly higher wealth taxes; inferred.

unions-good.rationale: Independent unions were banned and replaced by the state-run Vertical Syndicate, so adherents did not hold unions as such to be good.

property-fundamental.rationale: Private property is recognized and protected as a right, though conditioned by social function and the common good, so agreement but not strongly.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Doctrine subordinated all property to the common good, favoring state direction, yet the regime was friendly to big landowners and business; split.

cut-welfare.rationale: Church charity and social duty were stressed over dependency arguments; no documented drive to cut welfare, inferred from Catholic social duty.

worker-ownership.rationale: Labour was organized into state-run vertical syndicates of employers and workers, not worker-owned firms, and class-based ownership was rejected.

surveillance-ok.rationale: The regime relied on pervasive policing and gave parishes monitoring roles against perceived enemies, so surveillance for order was accepted.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the moral-order stance and the regime's criminalization of vice.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Hate-speech laws as modern liberal measures were not addressed; the regime censored speech for religious and moral reasons, not equal-dignity ones, so inferred disagreement.

strong-leader.rationale: Franco ruled as a personalist dictator for life and was held by the regime as the providential leader who bypassed parliamentary politics.

state-harmful.rationale: The regime upheld a strong state under law, with Catholic doctrine inspiring legislation; the anarchist view is the opposite.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed; the regime restricted civilian arms for security but no principled position exists, so neutral inferred.

empower-police-military.rationale: The Church and army were the pillars of power and the regime relied on repressive policing and military authority.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: The regime enforced strict Catholic sexual morality; the Women's Protection Board confined young women in Catholic-run centers.

decide-locally.rationale: Centralized unity was a core principle and regional languages and autonomy were suppressed; though municipalities are a basic structure in organic representation.

rehabilitation.rationale: The regime was punitive toward political opponents; Catholic doctrine allows rehabilitation, but the documented practice stressed punishment; inferred.

traditional-family.rationale: The Principles name the family as the basis of social life and the Fuero calls marriage one and indissoluble.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Homosexual acts were criminalized and suppressed; the family was defined as indissoluble Catholic marriage.

abortion-legal.rationale: Abortion, contraception and divorce were banned under the Catholic-based regime.

more-religion-public.rationale: National Catholicism is defined by the Church's hegemony over public and private life.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not a concern of the doctrine; inferred opposition from its stress on national unity and tradition over group-based remedies.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The regime promoted a fixed role for women as mothers and carers, grounded in natural and divine order, not social construction.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Catholic faith was fused with the national identity and Spanish tradition as the core of the regime's ideology.

gradual-change.rationale: The regime defended a restored order and was born of a violent counter-revolution; adherents prized tradition but did not value incrementalism as such.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Spain was a country of emigration then; not an issue of the doctrine, so neutral inferred.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The regime was isolated from the UN after WWII and asserted national sovereignty under a Catholic nation; later cooperation was pragmatic.

free-trade.rationale: Autarky was the policy through the 1940s and liberalization came late and from technocrats rather than from the doctrine.

nation-first.rationale: The doctrine fused nation and Catholic faith and the regime stressed Spain's distinctness from Europe, though universal Catholic ties limit pure nationalism.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Not addressed; the regime championed non-interference and Spanish sovereignty; inferred.

open-borders.rationale: A nation defined by Catholic unity and tradition does not hold borders should be open; inferred from the doctrine.

limit-growth.rationale: The regime ultimately pursued growth in the Spanish miracle; ecology was not addressed, so inferred disagreement.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic for the era; inferred from a technocratic growth orientation.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The doctrine put faith and moral order above technological hopes, though the later regime embraced technocracy; split.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Not addressed; later Francoist Spain did build nuclear power but doctrine is silent.

revolution-justified.rationale: Adherents saw the 1936 uprising as a crusade defending order, but the doctrine rejects revolution as a method; justified only against revolutionary regimes.

experts-over-public.rationale: The regime shifted to technocratic government and denied mass voting, with authority resting on organic structures and elites.

central-planning.rationale: Autarky involved heavy direction, but planning as superior to markets was not doctrine; the regime later abandoned it.

socialized-markets.rationale: Property is protected as private but socially conditioned; worker or public ownership is not doctrinal.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not addressed; the regime protected large landowners.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Family and property rights were upheld; heavy inheritance taxes are not documented, inferred.

basic-income.rationale: Unconditional income is unaddressed; the doctrine stresses duties and work, inferred.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Autarky and protectionism characterized the first decades of the regime.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The regime directed industry toward national self-sufficiency in the autarkic period via the state.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Catholic social teaching favors widespread property, but the regime protected large estates; inferred and contested.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Private property and a hierarchical social order were upheld; abolition of wages is counter to doctrine.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Not addressed; the regime maintained a national bank, inferred.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Labour and production were organized in state syndicates of employers and workers under the Fuero del Trabajo, though national syndicalism was more Falangist than clerical.

one-party-rule.rationale: The Movement was a single party, but National Catholics gave the Church a central role and saw the Falange as one pillar whose role Franco limited.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The Law of Succession declared Spain a kingdom and traditionalist Catholics favored monarchy, though Franco ruled as regent for life.

democracy-best.rationale: Liberal democracy was rejected and replaced with 'organic democracy', which sounded credible only to believers.

direct-votes.rationale: Representation was organic through family, municipality and syndicate, not through direct popular votes.

workers-councils.rationale: Revolutionary workers' councils were destroyed by the regime and political power was kept in Church, army and the Movement.

right-to-secede.rationale: The regime abolished regional autonomy and enforced unity of Spain; secession was treated as treason.

natural-rulers.rationale: A hierarchical, providential order where Franco and Church elites led; inferred from the personalist dictatorship.

political-violence-never.rationale: The regime was founded in a civil war it called a crusade and ruled by repression.

war-builds-character.rationale: Combat was valorized by the Falange and the regime, but Catholic doctrine on just war tempers it; split.

separate-church-state.rationale: The Concordat made Catholicism the sole legal religion, with state-appointed bishops and Church privileges.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Principle II holds that Catholic doctrine inspires legislation, though via Church doctrine and canon law rather than scripture itself.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The state held courts, force and defense; private provision is contrary to the doctrine of an authoritative state.

military-superiority.rationale: The army was a pillar of the regime, but Spain after 1939 was a weak, isolated power, so military superiority was not a stated aim.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Nationhood was defined by Catholic faith and Spanish unity rather than ethnicity; neutral.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Class conflict as history's driver is rejected; the regime used Catholic class-collaboration doctrine.

equal-outcomes.rationale: A hierarchical order with traditional roles is held; equality of outcomes is a socialist aim the regime suppressed.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from nationalist unity and Hispanidad's historic views.

colonial-reparations.rationale: The regime held Spain's imperial past as glorious and kept colonies, resisting decolonization until the 1950s and 60s.

civilizational-union.rationale: Hispanidad and Catholic civilization were themes, though a political union was not pursued; mild agreement.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Duty to the community and common good come before individual self-interest in Catholic and Francoist doctrine.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The Fuero de los Españoles pairs rights with duties and subordinates property and individuals to the nation and common good.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Not addressed; Catholic teaching sees nature as creation, giving some value; neutral.

limit-population.rationale: Contraception was banned and the regime promoted large families and motherhood.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Rural romanticism existed but the regime pursued industrialization and later the economic miracle.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Tradition and the existing order were prized over disruptive change.

human-enhancement.rationale: Catholic bodily morality and the regime's moral control argue against it; inferred.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the primacy of Catholic moral authority.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the surveillance state.

restore-past-order.rationale: Counter-revolution restoring Catholic Spain's traditional order was the regime's founding aim and National Catholicism's essence.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The regime's technocrats did govern pragmatically later, but the doctrine demanded fidelity to Catholic principles.

direct-action.rationale: The regime resorted to force to seize power but then opposed street action and strikes, which were banned.

means-match-ends.rationale: Not addressed as a principle; split.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Utterly alien to a Catholic civilizational order.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: A hierarchical, functionally organized society in syndicates is assumed.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Catholic charity and social function of property are doctrine, but distribution by need as a general system is a socialist aim; disagreement.

production-for-use.rationale: Property carries a social function and common good, but profit is permitted; split.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Marxist exploitation theory was rejected; class collaboration was the doctrine.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Communist rule was the enemy the regime defeated.

collective-farming.rationale: Collectivization during the war was reversed; landowners and small farmers were protected.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: A Marxist thesis rejected by the regime.

taxation-theft.rationale: Property is subordinate to the nation and common good; the state's authority to tax is legitimate.

harm-principle.rationale: The state restricted private moral conduct, censoring and enforcing Catholic marriage and sexual norms.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The family, municipality and syndicate were basic units with rights and duties; individualism was rejected.

conscription.rationale: The army was a regime pillar and military service was compulsory, with clergy exempt.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Not addressed; the regime restricted emigration at first and rejected elections as a check.

state-as-business.rationale: The state is a moral, national community under divine law, not a business.

positive-liberty.rationale: The Labour Fuero promised welfare and work as duties, but the language of freedom through material means was not used; split.

media-academia-power.rationale: The regime and Church saw liberal press and universities as corrupting forces, hence its control of both; inferred.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Doctrine was based on faith, not biological race; Catholic teaching rejects racial hierarchy.

organic-representation.rationale: Principle VIII and Fuero Article 10 set representation through family, municipality and syndicate.

total-state.rationale: Falangists wanted a total state, but National Catholics gave the Church an autonomous sphere over education and morals; internal Francoist split.

national-rebirth.rationale: The regime's founding story was the nation's regeneration from the decadence of the Republic.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Imperial rhetoric existed, but after 1939 Spain stayed neutral and lost colonies; split.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Franco's personalism had oath elements, but feudal oaths were not doctrine.

bound-labor.rationale: Catholic social teaching and the regime's Labour Fuero did not support serfdom.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Catholic doctrine holds that objective truth exists, and the regime imposed it in universities and schools.

universal-morality.rationale: Principle II holds the law of God according to Catholic doctrine as the standard for legislation.

single-common-good.rationale: Principles hold that individual and collective interests serve a common good set by Catholic doctrine, not by balancing parties.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Francoist Spain did not recognize Israel and was hostile to it, though not a doctrinal matter; Catholic teaching was cautious.

revive-national-language.rationale: The regime did not revive languages but imposed Spanish and suppressed others; inferred.

workplace-democracy.rationale: The syndicate was state-controlled with no democratic voice for workers.

school-vouchers.rationale: The Church wanted funding for its schools, which received generous aid, but voucher schemes were not documented.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Not addressed; the 1959 stabilization was austere, but doctrine silent.

economic-freedom.rationale: The regime held political freedom was not needed at all; economic liberalization came later without political liberalization.

rule-by-example.rationale: The ruler was to follow the law of God, but the regime relied on law and force; split.

national-self-determination.rationale: The regime defended Spanish national sovereignty, though denying it to Catalans and Basques within Spain.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Catholic faith is the foundation of the national identity; rationalism is rejected as secularism.

work-for-welfare.rationale: The Labour Fuero stressed work as duty; inferred.

class-collaboration.rationale: The syndicates united employers and workers under the Labour Fuero in the Catholic corporatist model.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Tradition and inherited culture, including Church heritage, are central.

dominated-front.rationale: The regime sought Western ties after isolation and joined with the US; no anti-Western front.

workers-nation.rationale: Workers were integrated into the national syndicates rather than an international class.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Women's role was centered on family; they could not be judges or open bank accounts without a male's signature.

ban-interest.rationale: Medieval Catholic usury doctrine was not part of regime policy, which allowed banking.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Faith not race defined the community, and Church teaching rejects racial segregation.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Marxist theory rejected; the state is an organic expression of the nation.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Autarkic policy sought domestic resources; inferred.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: National Catholic unity implies expectation to adopt Spanish Catholic culture; inferred.

elite-replacement.rationale: A modern conspiracy theory; not documented in the doctrine.

proportional-representation.rationale: Party-based representation was replaced by organic representation, so PR is irrelevant and rejected.

national-mission.rationale: Hispanidad and a Catholic mission for Spain, defender of the faith, were themes, though not about exporting government.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Gendered order was seen as natural and good, not as an unjust system.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The regime attacked republican politicians as corrupt, but ruled itself by elites; split.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Catholic doctrine opposes eugenic coercion, notwithstanding some Francoist psychiatry.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The regime never accounted for killings and the 1939 laws punished its enemies.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The state directs social life under divine law and guides family, property and labor.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Faith not race defined the community; Church doctrine rejects race-based marital bans.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Catholic doctrine affirms equal dignity before God, but the regime denied equal rights to women and opponents; contested.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Spain's own colonial history is viewed as civilizing; inferred.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Canon-law marriage was compulsory for Catholics, so civil law was not uniform; religion shaped law.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Article 6 allowed only private non-Catholic worship, with no outward manifestations, restricting proselytism.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Spanish Catholic culture includes eating beef; no sacred cow.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Catholic religious instruction was mandatory even in state schools.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Not applicable to a non-socialist state.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The regime's legitimacy rested on victory in the war and on God's law, not on elections; organic democracy was a label.

trade-surplus.rationale: Autarky favored self-sufficiency; inferred mercantile leaning.

population-transfer.rationale: Not documented as policy; Catholic teaching disapproves.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The regime originated in a military coup and war.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Social harmony and class collaboration were preferred to struggle.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: All parties other than the Movement were banned and repressed.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: A republican concept not addressed; the regime's strong authority contradicts it.

separated-powers.rationale: Power was concentrated in Franco as head of state and government for life.

vanguard-party.rationale: Marxist-Leninist idea, rejected as the enemy ideology.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Catholic social teaching and the Labour Fuero gave social justice a place, though regime practice favored the landed; contested.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Not addressed, though home ownership was promoted; neutral.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Strikes were banned and the vertical syndicate was the only legal union.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The regime promoted large families and did not hold this Malthusian view.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The doctrine stressed the unity of faith and nation as the basis of cohesion; inferred to apply to religious and cultural diversity.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Offices were held by appointment and organic structures.

party-controls-media.rationale: The 1938 Press Law imposed prior censorship and the Movement and state controlled news; the Church also had its own media.

party-commands-army.rationale: The army was a separate pillar led by Franco, not the party's; the Falange was subordinated.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Not a concern; no such demand.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: The Movement was a single organization but parties as such were rejected; neutral.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Spain was excluded from European institutions and the regime emphasised its distinctness from Europe.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Franco as head of state commanded the armed forces and named ministers.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Catholic hierarchy is episcopal, and the state held rights over bishop appointments.

clerical-rule.rationale: The Church dominated public life but did not rule directly; Franco and the army held power while clergy sat in institutions.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Rejects revolutionary defeatism, a communist position.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The Church could censor material under the Concordat and Church censors vetted cinema and books.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Franco held power for life with no elections.

recall-officials.rationale: Officials were appointed and answerable to Franco, not voters.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Spain made US base agreements in 1953; early policy was isolationist; split to disagreement.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Private property is recognized, abolition of rental is socialist.

people-in-arms.rationale: The professional army was the regime's pillar.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Rural life and large landowner protection characterized the regime's romanticism, and the rural colonization program; moderate agreement.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Gibraltar claim existed, but no divided nation per se; neutral.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The regime purged liberal teachers but valued its own educated elites; split.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Catholic civilization is seen as superior as true faith; cultural relativism is rejected.

death-penalty.rationale: The regime executed opponents on a large scale and had capital punishment through the end.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Schools were Catholicized and sex education and gender equality opposed.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Religious education in all schools was compulsory, but intelligent design as such is not documented; inferred.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Church-led censorship and moral control extended to sexual content.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Not documented, inferred from national identity.

minority-language-support.rationale: Regional languages lost official recognition and Spanish was required in schools and signage.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Non-Catholic worship was limited to private conduct and exemptions were not granted.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Social conformity to Catholic norms was enforced.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from property and legal order principles.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The constitution was a set of Fundamental Laws granted from above by the regime.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Political freedoms were suppressed while economic liberalization and growth were pursued in the 1960s.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Catholic charity favors aid but the doctrine did not make it a state duty; neutral.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Franco held the headship for life and the Law of Succession set the successor.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Not directly addressed; Gibraltar and other claims were maintained and Spain's territorial integrity was non-negotiable; inferred.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Principle X and Fuero Article 30 make property a right conditioned by social function and common good.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Not addressed; communism was condemned in itself.

collective-defense.rationale: The regime sought defense pacts with the US; no firm doctrine.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The Concordat gave the Church tax exemption, sanctuary, subsidies and autonomy.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The head of state was meant to be above parties, which were banned, though Franco led the Movement; monarchical tradition.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: The Civil War itself was waged for Spanish unity and the regime would use force against separatism.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Regional autonomy was abolished and uniformity imposed.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Franco ruled 'by the grace of God' with Church backing, but divine descent is not claimed.

character-from-environment.rationale: Catholic teaching stresses both nature and upbringing; neutral.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Principles bound legislation to divine law, though Franco held unchecked power; mixed.

mixed-constitution.rationale: The regime combined monarchy, army, Church and organic representation but did not espouse the theory; neutral.

leader-cult.rationale: Franco was honoured through portraits, statues, mass events and the NO-DO newsreels.

equal-parenting.rationale: Not addressed; traditional mother-centred family roles inferred.

land-redistribution.rationale: Republican land reform was reversed and rural colonization protected large landowners.

refugee-return.rationale: Not addressed; the regime exiled republicans, return was not welcomed.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Non-Catholics were tolerated in private belief and not molested, but leaving the faith was not criminalized; hostile public climate.

women-must-cover.rationale: The Church promoted modest dress but a legal covering mandate was not documented.

common-currency.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from nationalist sovereignty.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Hispanidad themes exist but political union was not pursued; neutral.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Historical materialism is rejected; Providence and faith are primary.

ban-cartels.rationale: The regime tolerated concentrated economic power; inferred.

no-bailouts.rationale: State support of industry was normal; inferred.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: No majority rule existed; courts were part of the state, with fundamental laws binding it.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Women were excluded from judgeships and subordinated in law.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Autarky was the regime's economic policy in the 1940s.

moral-incentives.rationale: The Labour Fuero stressed duty to work, but material incentives remained; neutral.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The regime claimed legitimacy from its army's uprising but rejects the revolution of the left.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The Law of Succession restored the monarchy and traditional hierarchy persisted.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Schools were Catholicized and nationalist history was taught.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Spain's colonial legacy was held as a civilizing mission; Spain resisted decolonization into the 1950s and 60s.

patriotic-education.rationale: Universities and schools were made to serve National Catholic principles with nation and flag.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The regime later liberalized and grew; inferred.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Hispanidad drew on Spain's Catholic empire for cultural influence in Latin America.

delink-world-market.rationale: Spain itself was autarkic then integrated; not a doctrine for poor countries.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Law bound private property to the common good, not absolute rights.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The Fuero listed rights but subordinated them to the Principles and national interest, and could be suspended.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Spain defended its colonial claims for decades; inferred.

elective-rulers.rationale: Succession was set by law, with Franco for life, then monarchy.

minority-veto.rationale: Unity and authority principles reject individual vetoes.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Traditional Catholic doctrine allows resistance to tyrants, but under Franco rebellion was condemned; contested.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The Cortes were organic and subordinate to the head of state.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Not addressed; Catholic teaching accepts some concern but mild.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Catholic teaching accepts use of animals with kindness; inferred.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Catholic social duty and charity were stressed for the privileged.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The nation's regeneration required active Catholic public life.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: The regime used mass culture for propaganda but doctrine did not hold the theory; neutral.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Gramscian thesis not addressed; the regime used both consent via Church and force.

native-born-offices.rationale: Inferred from national identity; Spain emphasised Spanish citizens.

party-own-road.rationale: Communist party strategy was not an issue for this doctrine, which opposed communism entirely; neutral.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: The autarkic policy of self-reliance in the 1940s; inferred as ideal.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Spaniards considered themselves civilizers; no deference to indigenous leadership.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: The regime itself was a fascist-influenced dictatorship; anti-fascism is its enemy.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: The regime condemned communism but not fascism; the equivalence not endorsed.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: The regime's monuments and symbols were its own; inferred preservation.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: The regime rejected liberal democracy, claiming organic democracy suited Spain's Catholic nature.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The army was a pillar of the regime and guardian of order.

paid-care-work.rationale: Women's family work was a duty and not paid labour; inferred.

filial-duty.rationale: The family is a natural institution with duties; inferred filial piety from Catholic doctrine.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Autarky limited foreign investment until the 1959 liberalization.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Marriage was to be one and indissoluble and divorce was banned.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Officials were not answerable to voters.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Collective social insurance was regime policy; inferred.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The Cortes were organic and subordinate to Franco.

single-official-language.rationale: Spanish was required in official documents, schools and signage and others were revoked.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Autarkic restrictions on foreign capital; inferred.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Catholic criticism of materialism; the regime's ideology valued austerity.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The regime suppressed opponents under war-time laws such as the 1939 Law of Political Responsibility, treating internal enemies as outside legal protection.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: The autarkic state rationed food and fixed prices in the 1940s, though rationing failed and famine followed.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred from the regime's censorship and hostility to foreign liberal and Protestant influence; no source documents a funding rule.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: The regime promoted large families and a high birth rate as part of its Catholic family ideal; the family is a protected institution in the Fundamental Laws.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred: the regime defended private property under a centralised unitary state, with no devolved power to reserve land for locals.

job-guarantee.rationale: Inferred from the Fuero del Trabajo's corporatist duty of the state toward workers; a formal guarantee as employer of last resort is not documented.

democratic-peace.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine rejected liberal democracy, so spreading it was not a peace programme.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: An authoritarian, hierarchical order under a providential leader expects obedience to lawful authority, though Catholic natural law allows that unjust laws do not bind.

non-intervention.rationale: Inferred from the regime's sovereigntist stance, though it also framed the war as a crusade against communism.

industrial-unions.rationale: The state's vertical syndicates organised employers and workers by branch of production, not by craft.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Regime rhetoric blamed a Masonic-communist conspiracy for Spain's ills; inferred from that propaganda rather than from the sources opened.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The Fuero de los Españoles declares marriage one and indissoluble and the Concordat required canonical marriage, so legal and religious marriage were central.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The state censored the press and kept official records secret; no right of access existed.

local-production.rationale: Inferred from the autarky of the early regime, which favoured national rather than local production.

informal-organisation.rationale: The doctrine favoured hierarchical, organic institutions (Church, state syndicates, single movement), not informal groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Inferred from the Francoist emphasis on national sovereignty; the Concordat nonetheless bound the state to Church law.

religious-nation.rationale: The defining idea is that Spanish identity is Catholic, and the state declared Catholicism its official religion.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Francoism stressed Spanish national sovereignty and the Hispanic tradition; inferred that it did not favour ritual submission to another power, although it relied on US aid after 1953.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: The regime was strongly centralist and suppressed regional autonomy; inferred that regions would not keep their revenue.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The Fuero del Trabajo and Fuero de los Españoles recognise and protect private property, so common ownership of production is rejected.

defeat-communism.rationale: Francoism presented itself as a crusade against communism and repressed its supporters, with the Church backing this.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: The Concordat gave the Church control of schools and charities within a state-supported system; inferred as agreement with mixed providers.

religion-illusion.rationale: National Catholicism made Catholic doctrine the basis of the state and held religion to be lasting and divinely grounded.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Inferred from corporatist and Catholic social teaching that criticised liberal capitalism and class conflict; no stated view on its progressive role.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Francoist law and the Church restricted women to the home and family and required male authority, rejecting economic transformation for equality.

socialized-care.rationale: The regime and the Church treated the family as the basis of society and women's place as domestic care, not public services.

purge-loanwords.rationale: The regime promoted Castilian and Spanish names and suppressed other languages; inferred mild support for purging foreign words, with no documented policy.

treaties-binding.rationale: Inferred from its centralist, unitary state that did not recognise national minorities nor treaties with them.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Inferred from its hierarchical, private-property and nation-state order, which rejects communal self-governing property.

majority-settlement.rationale: No settlement policy in minority regions is documented; the regime promoted Castilian unity, so this is a weak inference.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The Fuero del Trabajo and its corporatist syndicates were presented as an alternative to both liberal capitalism and Marxism.

missingStatements.text: Marriage should be indissoluble and regulated by religious law.
missingStatements.rationale: The Fuero de los Españoles declares marriage one and indissoluble and the Concordat required canonical marriage for Catholics.

missingStatements.text: The state should give one religion's institutions privileges and legal recognition not given to others.
missingStatements.rationale: Catholicism was the sole legally recognised religion with official protection, with other worship limited to private practice.

notes: Falangist strand favoured a total state and national syndicalism, so total-state and one-party answers are split; the economy moved from autarky to technocratic liberalization after 1959, so economic answers reflect the earlier period. Many answers on modern issues are inferred (low confidence).
